targetWords.definition: An accountant is a person whose job is to keep financial accounts.
targetWords.example: The accountant helped me keep track of my money. capitalist Eksepitelist] n.

targetWords.definition: —► The capitalist invested in a factory that made wheat into cereal.
targetWords.example: The capitalist invested in a factory that made wheat into cereal.

targetWords.definition: Contempt is the feeling of having no respect for something.
targetWords.example: The judge had contempt for the wicked criminal.

targetWords.definition: To dedicate oneself to something means to put a lot of time and effort into it.
targetWords.example: The nun dedicated herself to helping people in need. ditch [ditj] n.

targetWords.definition: —» When the car slid off of the road, it fell into the ditch.
targetWords.example: When the car slid off of the road, it fell into the ditch.

targetWords.definition: An enterprise is a company or business.
targetWords.example: My father owns an advertising enterprise.

targetWords.definition: When something is exquisite, it is very beautiful or pleasant.
targetWords.example: The artist made exquisite watercolor paintings.

targetWords.definition: To finance someone or something means to provide money for them.
targetWords.example: The government financed the scientist's experiments with new weapons.

targetWords.definition: When someone is indifferent toward something, they have a lack of interest in it.
targetWords.example: Lisa is indifferent toward school. She doesn't care what her final grades are.

targetWords.definition: To irrigate means to supply water to land so that crops can grow.
targetWords.example: In dry climates, it is important to irrigate fields of crops. UNIT

targetWords.definition: To maximize something is to make it as great in amount, size, or importance.
targetWords.example: You should exercise regularly to maximize a healthy lifestyle.

targetWords.definition: When something is monetary, it relates to money.
targetWords.example: A strong monetary policy is important for a country to be successful. precaution [prik6:Jan] n.

targetWords.definition: -* Asa precaution, you should put on a heavy coat before going out in cold weather.
targetWords.example: Asa precaution, you should put on a heavy coat before going out in cold weather.

targetWords.definition: Preliminary describes something that happens before a more important event.
targetWords.example: The runners must do well in the preliminary races to qualify for the final race.

targetWords.definition: To saturate something means to completely soak it with a liquid.
targetWords.example: The sponge was saturated with soapy water and dripped all over the floor.

targetWords.definition: The simplicity of something is the fact that it is easy to do or understand.
targetWords.example: We were able to find the house thanks to the simplicity of the directions.

targetWords.definition: To sow seeds means to plant them in the ground.
targetWords.example: He always sows his garden seeds in the springtime.

targetWords.definition: Soy is a food made from soybeans, such as flour or butter.
targetWords.example: Soy can be made into tofu, sauce, and also milk. S p a d e [speid] n.

targetWords.definition: —► The gardener used her spade to make a hole for the seed.
targetWords.example: The gardener used her spade to make a hole for the seed.

targetWords.definition: When something is upcoming, that means it will happen in the near future.
targetWords.example: The kids were worried about their upcoming exam.
